answer: He is able to find her before she comes home.
They watch storm from porch.
The man sits in a wooden bench.

category: avoids the practised grammar (Present Simple with now)
answer: Look! The assistant holds the reflector up now.
feedback_sk: Deje sa to teraz, patrí tu Present Continuous: „is holding“.
feedback_cz: Děje se to teď, patří sem Present Continuous: „is holding“.

answer: Wait a minute and the water will biol!
On the bench is one long bandage.
This ketchup is more thick than the sauce in the fridge.
The goalkeeper was standing on the line when the referee pointed to the penalty spot.
By the time the couple got their straws, he had put the umbrella on top.
If he will turn the ring once more, she will drop the price again.
feedback_sk: Po „if“ patrí v First Conditional Present Simple: „turns“, nie „will turn“.
feedback_cz: Po „if“ patří ve First Conditional Present Simple: „turns“, ne „will turn“.
feedback_other: In First Conditional use Present Simple after “if”: “turns”, not “will turn”.

answer: If he held the screwdriver, that shelf would by now on the floor be.
feedback_sk: Pozor na poradie slov: „be on the floor by now“.
feedback_cz: Pozor na pořadí slov: „be on the floor by now“.
feedback_other: Check the word order: “be on the floor by now”.

category: correct but avoids the practised grammar (active)
answer: They dipped the wooden paddle into the green water on both sides.
feedback_sk: Cvičenie precvičuje Passive: podmetom je pádlo, teda „the paddle was dipped“.
feedback_cz: Cvičení procvičuje Passive: podmětem je pádlo, tedy „the paddle was dipped“.
feedback_other: This exercise practises the Passive: the paddle is the subject, “the paddle was dipped”.

category: word order error (question order in a reported question)
answer: His flatmate asked him why did he spend two hours a day just to sit at a desk.
feedback_sk: V nepriamej otázke je slovosled ako v oznamovacej vete, bez „did/does“: „why he spent“.
feedback_cz: V nepřímé otázce je slovosled jako v oznamovací větě, bez „did/does“: „why he spent“.
feedback_other: In a reported question use statement word order, without “did/does”: “why he spent”.

answer: She managed staying completely still until the dragonfly settled.
feedback_sk: Po „manage“ vždy patrí Infinitive s „to“: „managed to stay“.
feedback_cz: Po „manage“ vždy následuje Infinitive s „to“: „managed to stay“.
feedback_other: “Manage” is always followed by the Infinitive with “to”: “managed to stay”.

answer: If he had added a whole fork, the dish would have been too hot to eat.

category: avoids the practised grammar (could + bare infinitive)
answer: She could laugh, but she just raised her eyebrows.
feedback_sk: Nevyužitá možnosť v minulosti je „could have“ + past participle: „could have laughed“.
feedback_cz: Nevyužitá možnost v minulosti je „could have“ + past participle: „could have laughed“.
feedback_other: A past chance that didn't happen needs “could have” + past participle: “could have laughed”.

answer: I wish my cat was as calm as that ginger one in her arms.
feedback_sk: V hovorovej reči sa „was“ používa, no po „wish“ je štandardné „were“.
feedback_cz: V hovorové řeči se „was“ používá, ale po „wish“ je standardní „were“.
feedback_other: “Was” is common in speech, but after “wish” the standard form is “were”.
